outcome.headline: The Novakai Messaging rebuild is finished: all four slices sealed, all six proof scenarios passing, 253 of 253 tests green.
outcome.summary: This session built the whole messaging capability from the frozen contracts: direct messages, rooms, push subscriptions, templates, two storage adapters, three transport adapters, and a standalone WebSocket mode for external chiefs. Every slice was pressure-tested by a fresh zero-context auditor before it was sealed, and every finding was fixed at the source with a regression test. The work is merged to main via PR #59.

changes.title: Contract types generated from one machine-readable source
changes.why: The project law is that every shape is defined once, so docs, code, and the visual map cannot drift apart.
changes.before: Contract shapes existed only in the design documents.
changes.after: TypeScript types and enums are generated from messaging-contract.json, and a test fails the build if the generated file drifts from the source.

changes.title: Durable store seam with memory and JSONL adapters
changes.why: Message acceptance has to be atomic and survive crashes; idempotent retry depends on it.
changes.before: There was no implementation at all.
changes.after: One atomic acceptance transaction, global sequence ordering, cursor pagination, and crash recovery support. The same contract test suite runs against both adapters, including concurrent-writer cases.

changes.title: Core send path with one decision point
changes.why: All policy decisions belong in one place so no caller can accidentally bypass them.
changes.after: Sends are parsed from unknown input at the door, decided in one module, committed atomically, and delivered through the R5 state machine with DND holds, retries, and terminal failure.

changes.title: Push subscriptions and standalone WebSocket mode
changes.why: The whole point of the rebuild: external chiefs get pushed events and never poll.
changes.before: The old app made chiefs run 20-minute mailbox-scan crons.
changes.after: Events are emitted only after they are durable, subscribers replay from a cursor after disconnect, and a standalone WebSocket server lets any external terminal connect.

changes.title: Rooms through the membership seam
changes.why: Team and mission messages need one message with a frozen snapshot of who was a member at send time.
changes.after: Room sends resolve membership fresh at acceptance, freeze the recipient snapshot, and blocked recipients fail terminally at commit time rather than ever receiving the message.

changes.title: Templates and the PTY transport adapter
changes.why: Templates complete the public contract, and the PTY adapter finishes the adapter-swap proof.
changes.before: Template commands were defined in the contract but not implemented.
changes.after: Templates render only into allowlisted message paths, retirement is permanent, and one shared transport test suite passes unchanged against the memory, PTY, and WebSocket adapters.

decisions.title: The contract JSON stayed frozen after Step 2
decisions.rationale: Everything the build later needed was added as numbered, dated errata in the store-seam document instead of editing the frozen contract. The drift guard and codegen kept one source of truth the whole way through.

decisions.title: Blocked room messages fail at commit time, not afterwards
decisions.rationale: The S2 auditor proved a blocked recipient could still receive a message in the gap between commit and the post-commit effect pass. The fix makes the block terminal inside the same atomic commit, so no later code path can ever see the blocked delivery as sendable.

decisions.title: One runtime dependency
decisions.rationale: The whole package runs on a single dependency (the ws WebSocket library). Everything else is Node built-ins, which keeps the supply chain small and the harness dependency-free.

problems.problem: The JSONL store adapter was not atomic under concurrency: two retries of the same message could both be accepted.
problems.resolution: The S1 auditor reproduced it with real concurrent calls. Every store mutation now goes through a per-store queue, and the regression tests were shown to fail before the fix and pass after.

problems.problem: A ContactPolicy-blocked room recipient could still be delivered the message through two ordinary timing interleavings.
problems.resolution: The S2 auditor reproduced both paths. The block is now applied terminally inside the atomic commit, which removes the vulnerable window entirely.

problems.problem: Template field checks could be bypassed through JavaScript's prototype chain, letting a declared field silently vanish at render time.
problems.resolution: The S4 auditor reproduced it. Field matching now uses own-key checks and prototype-related names are rejected from the allowlist, with regression tests.

artifacts.title: A runnable messaging package with 253 green tests
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: The @novakai/messaging package works in two modes: embedded in a host app, or standalone over WebSocket for external chiefs. All six planned proof scenarios pass, including crash-recovery tests that SIGKILL the server mid-flight.

artifacts.title: A second-host example messenger
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: examples/messenger-cli is a small terminal messenger that talks to the standalone server using only the published protocol. It proves a second host can use the capability without importing any of its code.

artifacts.title: Audit records and the quality scorecard
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: Every slice has a written audit record (Messaging-S1 through S4 review documents) showing what the independent auditor found and how each finding was fixed. The final scorecard rates the capability 97.0 out of 100 against the elite rubric.

artifacts.title: Merged to main
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: The full program is on the main branch of novakai-command via pull request #59, with one commit per sealed slice so the history stays readable.
